subject: Kepler: post-call deep-dive recap — latency & throughput SLOs + topology
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@kepler.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kepler: post-call deep-dive recap — latency & throughput SLOs + topology

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have a shared record and clear next steps. I focused this on the three items your engineering team asked us to confirm: production latency SLOs, throughput/burst model, and deployment topology (private vs. dedicated).

Key pain points you reiterated
- Real-time scoring for customer-facing features: 95th pct latency target of 120–180ms for single-turn LLM calls (90ms preferred for high-priority routes).
- High request volume variability (seasonal spikes ~5–6x baseline) with tight cost controls.
- Regulatory requirement: model inputs cannot leave Kepler VPC for PII routes (so private deployment for PII-bound traffic).

Goals we aligned on
- Pilot: 3-week pilot covering 2 routes (customer query routing + risk scoring) at 50 RPS baseline with burst to 300 RPS.
- SLOs: 95th pct <= 180ms for non-PII; 99th pct <= 300ms for PII (accounting for VPC egress overhead).
- Success criteria: latency within SLO for 95% of requests during steady-state and graceful degradation during bursts (fallback to lower-cost model variant).

Technical assumptions called out
- Model: you indicated preference for an open 7B/13B family with quantization to int8 for cost controls; we will validate top-k/top-p tuning impact on latency.
- KV caching: we recommended prefix caching for repeated prompts in the risk-scoring route to reduce end-to-end latency.
- Networking: private deployment will use our Private control plane + customer peering (no model traces leave the VPC).

Attachments I’m including
- kepler-slo-matrix.xlsx (SLO baseline, test cases, and proposed monitoring hooks)
- redwood-deploy-topology-v1.png (sketch: mixed routing — PII -> Private cluster; non-PII -> Hosted/Dedicated with cost-aware routing)

Open questions / asks for Kepler engineers
1) Can you confirm typical payload sizes (avg tokens in + expected returned tokens) for each route? We used 250 tokens in our sizing.
2) Any network egress bandwidth constraints or preferred peering time windows we should plan around for the private deploy?
3) Do you have an internal compliance contact we should loop in for the VPC onboarding checklist (KMS, audit logs)?

Proposed next steps (timeline)
- This week: Kepler supplies payload sizes + compliance contact (we’ll get the VPC checklist ready).
- Week 1: Redwood provision pilot topology (private + dedicated), run baseline and synthetic load tests.
- Week 2: Joint validation with live traffic shadowing, measure SLOs and KV cache hit-rates.
- Week 3: Optimize batching/quantization and agree on handoff to Kepler infra for production run.

If that aligns, I’ll request a quick calendar block for the provisioning prep (30m) with your infra lead and Naomi (she’ll own the topology on our side).

Thanks — forwardable to your team.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachment: kepler-slo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Diego — thanks, this is helpful and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Payloads: customer query avg input ~120 tokens, expected output ~60 tokens. Risk-scoring route average input ~40 tokens, output ~10 tokens. Peak bursts have larger batched requests from downstream batchers (up to ~800 tokens aggregate).
- For PII: we need E2E encryption and customer-managed KMS. We have an internal Compliance lead (Priya Rao — priya.rao@kepler.ai) — please loop her into the VPC checklist.
- Cost sensitivity: we’re deciding between using Dedicated nodes during business hours and Hosted for off-hours. Can Redwood’s routing switch automatically based on capacity/SLOs?

Also: curious if you can surface an initial cost delta between all-hosted vs mixed private+dedicated for the pilot (ballpark is fine). If you can share a quick pricing sketch, I’ll pass to our procurement.

On the calendar block: Tuesday 8/31 10:00am PT works for our infra lead if that helps.

—Sam

CTO, Kepler Analytics

Sam / Priya — looping you in, and attaching an initial cost sketch and the SLO matrix updated with your payload numbers. Quick points: 

1) Confirmed sizing updates (using your token counts):
   - Customer query route: baseline 50 RPS -> estimate Dedicated pool: 4 x A10-equivalent for target latency headroom; burst to 300 RPS handled with burst capacity + intelligent routing to hosted pool.
   - Risk scoring route: baseline 30 RPS (small payloads) -> fits onto Dedicated batching-optimized instances; KV cache expected to reduce token compute by ~30% for repeated keys.

2) Routing capabilities: yes — Redwood supports policy-based routing. We can configure:
   - PII traffic: always route to Private cluster (VPC peering + CMK).
   - Non-PII: route by latency budget and cost threshold; when Dedicated nears 80% CPU, traffic spills to Hosted compatible variant. Automatic fallbacks available.

3) Compliance / onboarding: Priya, Naomi will follow up with the VPC/KMS checklist and an initial network runbook. Naomi — can you confirm earliest availability for the provisioning call on Tue 8/31 10:00am PT?

4) Cost sketch: attached (ballpark monthly run-rate for pilot):
   - All-hosted (no private): ~$12k–16k/mo (higher per-token but no infra setup)
   - Mixed private + dedicated (recommended): ~$8k–12k/mo + one-time setup (~$4k) — depends on committed capacity and KV cache effectiveness.
